newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian Fortis asset management group favours cash.
newsitem.headline: Belgian Fortis asset management group favours cash.

text.p: Asset management group Fortis Investments Belgium said on Thursday that in the longer term it expected the dollar to weaken, U.S. interest rates to rise and it saw no sign of decoupling between U.S. and European bonds.

As a result its favoured investment strategy was to be underweight in bonds, overweight in cash and take neutral weighting on equities, FIB's head of research Dirk De Batselier told an FIB institutional investors seminar in Brussels.
"U.S. economic growth is strong, though decelerating, and inflation will be a fear for the Federal Reserve," De Batselier said.

He predicted the Fed would raise short term rates in the first part of 1997. U.S. capacity utilisation and unemployment rates were close to levels historically seen at times of inflation. Commodity prices should also be watched carefully.

"We see short and long term U.S. rates rising. Long term U.S. interest rates went up in 1994 even when there was no inflation because the Fed raised its short term rates after strong economic data," he added.
De Batselier said in Europe recovery was under way but there was no inflationary pressure.

Comparing long term U.S. and German bond yields showed an 87 percent correlation between the two historically so there was no reason to expect a decoupling in the future, and Bund yields could therefore be expected to rise too.

Once the planned single European currency was introduced and bonds were quoted in Euros, Belgian OLOs could expect to have a normal yield spread over Bunds of between 15 and 20 basis points reflecting Belgium's credit risk, De Batselier said.
The spread is currently back at 16 bp after narrowing a few weeks ago to around six as the market became over enthusiastic at the prospect of a single currency.
His target for the U.S. dollar was a trading range of 1.50 to 1.55 marks on a three-month horizon, weakening to 1.45 marks in 12 months time.
On equities De Batselier was positive on Europe and neutral on Japan, both of which were still attractive versus bond yields, and negative on the U.S. market.
Fortis Investment Belgium is the Belgian asset management unit of Belgian-Dutch insurance and banking group Fortis AMEV.AS, and was set up in June this year.
